name: Kamaru
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Glottolog ref: van den Berg 2008 'Notes on the historical phonology and classification of Wolio' (Lincom, offline) — comparative, not a Kamaru description; no grammar/phonology of Kamaru found online.

sources.citation: Firman A.D. 2017. Bahasa Lasalimu-Kamaru: kajian dialektologi. Telaga Bahasa 5(1): 17-36. DOI 10.36843/tb.v5i1.118
sources.note: Dialectometry on 200+87 items from four villages (Lasalimu, Kamaru, Lawele, Kekenauwe); concludes Lasalimu-Kamaru is one language with three dialects (Kamaru, Lasalimu, Kekenauwe-Lawele) and lists sound correspondences (t≈c, p≈f, o≈a, r≈x..). Transcriptions mark vowel length (ba:tu, ku:tu) but no stress; no word 'tekanan'/'aksen' anywhere.

sources.citation: Sanjoko, Yohanis. 2015. Kata penyukat dalam bahasa kerabat Lasalimu dan Kamaru (Measurement words in related language Lasalimu and Kamaru). Metalingua 13(2): 261-272. DOI 10.26499/metalingua.v13i2.11
sources.note: Classifier morphology/syntax only; no phonology, no stress statement. Its introduction (p. 262) cites Nusi 2012 (UGM thesis) as covering Lasalimu-Kamaru 'dari sisi fonologi dan leksikon' and Firman A.D. 2012 (in Yamaguchi ed.) on the three dialects.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2004. The pretenders to the Muna-Buton group. In John Bowden & Nikolaus Himmelmann (eds), Papers in Austronesian subgrouping and dialectology (Pacific Linguistics 563), 21-35. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. DOI 10.15144/PL-563.21
sources.note: Comparative paper presenting Kamaru wordlist data ('the previously undescribed Kamaru language of eastern Buton', p. 27) for subgrouping; the only stress remark is fn. 2 (p. 21) on the local pronunciation of the island name 'Butung' being 'stressed on the second syllable' — nothing on Kamaru word stress.

tone.quote: Namun, realisasi vokal panjang pada bahasa Lasalimu bukan merupakan fonemis melainkan fonetis semata. Dalam berkomunikasi panjang pendeknya vokal yang diproduksi oleh penutur tidak menjadi hambatan dalam pemahaman satu sama lain. Tampaknya vokal panjang itu terjadi karena pengucapan logat setempat (kolektif idiolek) yang diakibatkan karena terdapat tekanan pada suku kata penultima yang cenderung pengucapan vokalnya agak dipertahankan temponya sehingga terkesan ada perpanjangan vokal tertentu.
tone.locator: p. 64, section 'Kontras Vokal dan Variannya', right column
tone.translation: However, the realisation of long vowels in Lasalimu is not phonemic but merely phonetic. In communication, the length of the vowels produced by speakers is no obstacle to mutual understanding. The long vowels apparently arise from the local accent (collective idiolect), caused by there being stress on the penultimate syllable, whose vowel tends to be held somewhat longer in pronunciation, so that certain vowels give the impression of lengthening.
tone.citation_as_reported: Sanjoko, Yohanis. 2015. Perbandingan karakteristik fonem bahasa Indonesia dengan bahasa Lasalimu (Comparative characteristics of Indonesian and Lasalimu language phonemes). Kandai 11(1): 55-67. Kendari: Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Sulawesi Tenggara. DOI 10.26499/jk.v11i1.216
